raw_response:
I will keep things simple and steady. I am 78, so I do not want crops that need too much hand labor or too much watching every day. In Quzhou, I know wheat and maize best, and this rotation fits my land, my habits, and the local weather. Wheat gives me a stable grain crop through the cooler season, and after harvest I can follow with summer maize on the same land. I will not spread myself across many crops, because that raises risk and work. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, put on moderate fertilizer instead of chasing the highest yield, irrigate when the crop really needs it, and spray only a few times when pressure is clear. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and more familiar than full no-tillage. My goal is not the maximum yield. My goal is a crop I can finish well, with lower labor pressure and dependable output.
